name: Randomized $k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension
definition: For an integer $k\geq0$, the **Randomized $k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension** is $\mathrm{RL}^{\mathrm{mist}}_k(\mathcal H)=\frac12\sup_T\mathbb E_T$, where T ranges over binary decision trees whose every branch disagrees with some hypothesis in $\mathcal H$ on at most k queried labels, and $\mathbb E_T$ is the random root-to-leaf length.
graph_summary: Half the largest average branch length of a tree whose paths are realizable with at most k mistakes.
origin_references: Introduced by Filmus, Hanneke, Mehalel, and Moran \cite{filmus2023randomized}.

monotonic.proof: Every k-shattered tree for a subfamily is also k-shattered by the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: A k-shattered tree for a projection queries only retained coordinates; lifting its realizing projected hypotheses preserves every branch's number of disagreements.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: For an active one-coordinate split, c-monotonicity gives a value at least the larger branch value, hence strictly above the smaller one when they differ. If the branch values agree, attach near-optimal k-shattered trees below a root querying the split coordinate. The root agrees with the branch condition, so it adds no disagreement and raises the randomized value by one half.

strictly_monotonic.proof: The parameter is doubly monotonic and strictly c-monotonic; its value can vanish only for a class with at most one hypothesis.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: At k=0, the two constant hypotheses have singleton conditioned branches, both of value 0, while the whole class has randomized k-mistake Littlestone dimension 1/2 rather than 1. Thus the equal-branch +1 condition fails.
